info.title: Rebase PRs against origin/main for CI green

parts.text: There are a bunch of open PRs that needs to be rebased against origin/main and ultimately get their CI green. Your objective is to pick up all currently existing PRs and go over them one-by-one, on a separate git worktree for each, then push again to same branch where needed, with force, so that they're each ready to be merged, with green CI. Plan your work. Remmeber that it's key that you don't disrupt the intended value increment of the PR, but rather mtigiate conflicts.

Let me understand the task:

1. I need to pick up all currently existing PRs
2. Go over them one-by-one on a separate git worktree for each
3. Push again to the same branch where needed, with force
4. Make sure CI is green for each
5. The goal is to have each PR ready to merge

First, I need to understand what PRs exist. Let me start by exploring the repository structure and finding open PRs.

state.output:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      # The site is generated and committed so a reviewer can read the
      # rendered HTML in a pull request. If the committed copy no longer
      # matches a fresh build, the site has drifted and the PR is not ready.
      - name: Check the committed site matches a fresh build
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --check

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --out _site

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

        run: |

          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7

          node-version: "lts/*"

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle

        env:

            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build

            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |

            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      # The site is generated and committed so a reviewer can read the
      # rendered HTML in a pull request. If the committed copy no longer
      # matches a fresh build, the site has drifted and the PR is not ready.
      - name: Check the committed site matches a fresh build
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --check

 from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.memory import StudioMemory
 from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.router import router as studio_router
 
 CORS_ORIGINS = [
     "tauri://localhost",
     "http://tauri.localhost",
     "http://localhost:5173",
     "http://127.0.0.1:5173",
     "http://localhost:8100",
     "http://127.0.0.1:8100",
 ]
 
 DEFAULT_BACKEND = "local"
 
 
 def default_spa_dist() -> Path:
     """Resolve the built SPA, preferring an explicit override."""
     configured = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST")
     if configured:
         return Path(configured)
     return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "apps" / "studio" / "dist"
 
 
 SPA_DIST = default_spa_dist()
 
 
 def create_app(
     repo: Repository | None = None,
     backend: str | None = None,
     connectors: ConnectorService | None = None,
     memory: StudioMemory | None = None,
 ) -> FastAPI:
     if repo is None:
         repo = SQLiteRepository()
     service = ODIService(repo)
     app = FastAPI(title="Agentic ODI Studio API")
     app.state.service = service
     app.state.backend = backend or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND") or DEFAULT_BACKEND
     app.state.connectors = connectors or ConnectorService()
     app.state.memory = memory or StudioMemory()
 
     app.add_middleware(
         CORSMiddleware,
         allow_origins=CORS_ORIGINS,
         allow_credentials=False,
         allow_methods=["*"],
         allow_headers=["*"],
     )
 
     @app.get("/health")
     def health() -> dict:
         return {"status": "ok"}
 
     @app.get("/capabilities")
     def capabilities() -> dict:
         return {"capabilities": app.state.backend}
 
     app.include_router(studio_router)
 
     if SPA_DIST.is_dir() and not os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DISABLE_SPA"):
         assets_dir = SPA_DIST / "assets"
         if assets_dir.is_dir():
             app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=assets_dir), name="assets")
 
         @app.get("/{full_path:path}", response_model=None)
         def spa_fallback(full_path: str) -> FileResponse | JSONResponse:
+            if full_path.startswith("api/"):
+                return JSONResponse({"detail": "Not Found"}, status_code=404)
             candidate = (SPA_DIST / full_path).resolve()
             if full_path and candidate.is_file() and candidate.is_relative_to(SPA_DIST.resolve()):
                 return FileResponse(candidate)
             index = SPA_DIST / "index.html"
             if index.is_file():
                 return FileResponse(index)
             return JSONResponse({"detail": "Not Found"}, status_code=404)
 
     return app

 # CLI Reference
 
 The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
 command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
 provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
 commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
 required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
 
 Install the workspace first if you have not already:
 
 ```bash
 uv sync --all-packages
 ```
 
 ## Launching
 
 ```bash
 python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
 python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
 python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
 ```
 
 A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
 
 ## Global options
 
 | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
 | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
 | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
 
 Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
 machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
 (`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
 
 ## Interactive chat
 
 `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
 offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
 MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
 and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.
 
 ```bash
 agentic-odi chat
 agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
 ```
 
 ### Connection settings
 
 The chat resolves settings in priority order:
 **CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**
 
 | Variable | Default | CLI flag |
 |---|---|---|
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
 
 The **persisted profile** is stored at
 `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
 within the session using `/connect`.
 
 ### Slash commands
 
 | Command | Description |
 |---|---|
 | `/help` | Show all available commands |
 | `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
 | `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
 | `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
 | `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
 | `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
 | `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
 | `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |
 
 ### /connect wizard
 
 `/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:
 
 1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
 2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
 3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
 4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
 5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
 6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions
 
 The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
 > and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
 
 ## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes
 
 Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
 the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
 Job cascades to both.
 
 ```bash
 # Jobs
 agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
 agentic-odi jobs list
 agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
 agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
 agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
 
 # Steps (Job Map)
 agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
 agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
 agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
 agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
 
 # Desired Outcomes
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 ```
 
 Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.
 
 ## Evidence
 
 Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
 a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
 artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.
 
 ```bash
 # Capture a record by hand
 agentic-odi evidence add \
   --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
   --name "Support lead" \
   --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
   --job-id <job-id>
 
 # Read and delete
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
 agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
 agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
 
 # Promote into the ODI model
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
 ```
 
 `connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
 ingested batch into evidence in one step.
 
 ## Schema and scoring
 
 ```bash
-agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
-agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+agentic-odi schema                   # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi framework-guidelines     # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide
+agentic-odi capabilities             # what the assistant can help with
+agentic-odi score 8 2                # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
 ```
 
 ## Manage Customer Outcomes
 
 Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
 writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
 to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
 available under its historical name `outcomes`.
 
 ```bash
 # Add a Customer Outcome
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
   --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
 
 # Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
   --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
 
 # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
 
 # Get, update, delete
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 
 # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
 agentic-odi score 8 2
 agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
 ```
 
 `score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
 `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
 
 Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
 using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 
 ## Connectors
 
 The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
 [External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
 ingest behavior.
 
 ```bash
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
 ```
 
 ## Updates
 
 `odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
 default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
 `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

 # Roadmap & Next Steps
 
 As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:
 
 - [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an
   HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
 - [x] **Conversational rich surfaces**: the studio agent composes validated
   cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them
   in prose.
 - [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into
   jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI
   store.
 - [x] **First-run wizard**: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline
   connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context
   conversation — isolated in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/` behind the
   `firstRunWizard` flag.
 - [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations
   implementing the same `Connector` protocol.
 - [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*,
   *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
 - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `apps/cli` so the ODI dataset can be
   created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current
   MCP path.
 - [x] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like
   `get_job_map(job_id)`, `get_outcomes(job_id)`, `get_step(step_id)`,
   `get_outcome(outcome_id)`, or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
 - [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight
   SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
 - [x] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the
   `openai` package) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently
   request customer insights when ideating features.
+
+## Upcoming
+
+The validated milestones above are complete. Next candidates for the backlog:
+
+- **CLI parity surface**: expose every MCP tool (including

+  commands so the terminal mirrors the server.

+  actionable message instead of raw exceptions.
+- **Coverage**: keep the test suite at or above the 90% Codecov target as new
+  tools and commands land.

+"""Tests for outcome-statement evaluation."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from agentic_odi_core.evaluation import evaluate_outcome_statement
+
+
+def test_valid_maximize_statement_passes() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement(
+        "Maximize the conversion rate when onboarding a new customer."
+    )
+    assert result["valid"] is True
+    assert result["direction"] == "maximize"
+    assert result["issues"] == []
+
+
+def test_valid_minimize_statement_passes() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement(
+        "Minimize the time to resolve a support ticket before the customer churns."
+    )
+    assert result["valid"] is True
+    assert result["direction"] == "minimize"
+    assert result["issues"] == []
+
+
+def test_missing_direction_reports_issue() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement("The conversion rate when onboarding.")
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert result["direction"] is None
+    assert any("Minimize" in issue or "Maximize" in issue for issue in result["issues"])
+
+
+def test_vague_term_reports_issue() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement("Improve the onboarding flow when a user signs up.")
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert any("improve" in issue.lower() for issue in result["issues"])
+
+
+def test_too_short_statement_reports_issue() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement("Maximize it.")
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert any("too short" in issue for issue in result["issues"])
+
+
+def test_overly_long_statement_reports_issue() -> None:
+    long_statement = "Maximize " + ("the metric " * 40) + "when doing something."
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement(long_statement)
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert any("200 characters" in issue for issue in result["issues"])
+
+
+def test_missing_context_reports_issue() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement("Maximize the conversion rate.")
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert any("context" in issue for issue in result["issues"])
+
+
+def test_suggestions_are_provided_for_invalid() -> None:
+    result = evaluate_outcome_statement("Improve things when possible.")
+    assert result["valid"] is False
+    assert result["suggestions"]

/connect Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save
/model <name> Hot-swap to a different model mid-session
/mcp <url> Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session
/tools List the MCP tools the assistant can call
/clear Reset conversation history (keeps connection)
/exit Quit the session (also /quit)

/connect wizard

/connect walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:

  1. Provider — choose openai, anthropic, local, or other
  2. Base URL — preset filled for known providers; override freely
  3. API key — input is hidden via getpass
  4. Model — sensible default per provider
  5. MCP URL — defaults to the current value
  6. Save to profile? — writes ~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json so settings persist across sessions

The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.

[!NOTE] Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The customer-outcomes and connectors commands keep working without one.

Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes

Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a Job cascades to both.

# Jobs
 agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
 agentic-odi jobs list
 agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
 agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
 agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
 
 # Steps (Job Map)
 agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
 agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
 agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
 agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
 
 # Desired Outcomes
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
 agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

Add --json to any command for machine-readable output.

Evidence

Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.

# Capture a record by hand
 agentic-odi evidence add \
   --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
   --name "Support lead" \
   --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
   --job-id <job-id>
 
 # Read and delete
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
 agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
 agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
 
 # Promote into the ODI model
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
 agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>

connectors ingest --job-id <job-id> maps every evidence-bearing record in the ingested batch into evidence in one step.

Schema and scoring

-
agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
-agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+
agentic-odi schema                   # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi framework-guidelines     # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide
+agentic-odi capabilities             # what the assistant can help with
+agentic-odi score 8 2                # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
 
Manage Customer Outcomes

 
Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The local backend
 writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add --backend mcp
 to route through a running MCP server (python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server). The group is also
 available under its historical name outcomes.

 
# Add a Customer Outcome
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
   --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
 
 # Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
   --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
 
 # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
 
 # Get, update, delete
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 
 # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
 agentic-odi score 8 2
 agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
 
score applies the ODI opportunity formula,
 importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0).

 
Set AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL (or --mcp-url) to point to a non-default server when
 using --backend mcp (default: http://localhost:8000/mcp).

 
Connectors

 
The connectors group manages external MCP integrations. See
 External Connectors for presets, the connector registry, and
 ingest behavior.

 
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
 python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
 
Updates

 
odi update checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
 default; disable it with --no-update for one run or
 AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1 globally. See Installation.

Roadmap & Next Steps

What has shipped, and what is queued.

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

  • [x] External MCP client connector: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
  • [x] Conversational rich surfaces: the studio agent composes validated cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them in prose.
  • [x] Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store.
  • [x] First-run wizard: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context conversation — isolated in apps/studio/src/onboarding/ behind the firstRunWizard flag.
  • [x] Additional connector kinds: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same Connector protocol.
  • [x] ODI Schema Definition: Define standardized Pydantic models for Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes.
  • [x] CLI Dataset Commands: Extend apps/cli so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
  • [x] Context Tooling: Replace the dummy greet tool with capabilities like get_job_map(job_id), get_outcomes(job_id), get_step(step_id), get_outcome(outcome_id), or evaluate_outcome(statement).
  • [x] Data Persistence Layer: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
  • [x] Agentic Integration: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the openai package) so the LLM can discover the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

1: """Conversational helper with offline fallbacks and a streaming tool loop.
2: 
3: The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
4: ``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
5: intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
6: catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
7: suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
8: writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.
9: 
10: The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
11: and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
12: """

47: SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an elite product strategist working inside The Living Studio, a room built for product managers.
48: Your job is to help the PM choose and win the next opportunity that matters — to customers, the business, and their career.
49: Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) is your private engine, not the conversation. Translate the PM's ambition into jobs, outcomes, and evidence silently, and speak in the PM's language.
50: 
51: How to work:
52: 1. Start with the person and the stakes. Ask what opportunity they are chasing, who it is for, and what winning would change. One good question at a time.
53: 2. Mirror their words back, then offer a sharp hypothesis they can correct.
54: 3. When they give you context worth keeping — a career goal, a constraint, a stakeholder, a belief — call `remember` with the smallest useful observation. Do not ask permission first; the UI lets them confirm, edit, or dismiss it.
55: 4. Use ODI when it earns its keep: a job statement clarifies, a desired outcome sharpens, an opportunity score compares. Never lead with the framework or lecture about stages.
56: 5. Opportunity Score = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0). Above 10 means underserved.
57: 6. When a surface carries the evidence better than a paragraph, call `render_ui` once, then write one short sentence. Never describe in prose what a card can already show.
58: 7. The conversation is the product: every surface you render lands in the thread the PM is already reading. Never tell them to open a panel, a tab, or a view to see something you can show inline.
59: 8. Capture and simulation are conversations, not forms: ask for the customer's words or the bet in plain language, render the card that carries it, and offer the next move as an action on that card.
60: 9. When asked to add or query Jobs, Steps, or Outcomes, ALWAYS invoke the corresponding tools.
61: 10. Be warm, direct, and specific. Short sentences. No corporate jargon, no therapy-speak, no emojis."""

107:             "3. **Score the opportunity** — `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`; above 10 is underserved.\n"

109:             "Type `/capture` to record an outcome, `/jobmap` to walk the phases, "

131:         "- `/jobmap` — add or edit the steps of the job\n"
132:         "- `/landscape` — review what is underserved\n\n"

252: def _apply_add_connector(
253:     arguments: dict[str, Any], service: ConnectorService
254: ) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
255:     """Register a connector locally and return SSE event dicts for the stream."""
256:     name = arguments.get("name")
257:     preset_id = arguments.get("preset")
258:     url = arguments.get("url")
259:     try:
260:         config = service.add(name=name, preset_id=preset_id, url=url)
261:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
262:         event = {"event": "connector", "data": {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}}
263:         return f"Error: {exc}", [event]
264:     event_data: dict[str, Any] = {"action": "registered", "name": config.name}
265:     if preset_id is not None:
266:         event_data["preset"] = preset_id
267:     if url is not None:
268:         event_data["url"] = url
269:     return f"registered connector {config.name}", [{"event": "connector", "data": event_data}]

272: def _apply_remember(
273:     arguments: dict[str, Any], memory: StudioMemory | None
274: ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
275:     """Store one suggested observation without asking the PM first."""
276:     if memory is None:
277:         return "Memory is not available to this client.", None
278: 
279:     kind = str(arguments.get("kind", ""))
280:     text = str(arguments.get("text", ""))
281:     data = arguments.get("data")
282:     try:
283:         confidence = float(arguments.get("confidence", 0.6))
284:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
285:         confidence = 0.6
286: 
287:     try:
288:         observation = memory.add_observation(
289:             kind=kind,
290:             text=text,
291:             data=data if isinstance(data, dict) else None,
292:             status="suggested",
293:             confidence=confidence,
294:         )
295:     except ValueError as exc:
296:         return f"Could not remember that: {exc}", None
297:     return "Saved for the user to review.", {"observation": observation.to_dict()}

332:     for tool_call in delta.tool_calls or []:

334:         if tool_call.id:
335:             entry["id"] = tool_call.id
336:         if tool_call.function is not None:
337:             if tool_call.function.name:
338:                 entry["name"] = tool_call.function.name
339:             if tool_call.function.arguments:

343: def _persist_turn(
344:     memory: StudioMemory | None, conversation_id: str | None, role: str, content: str
345: ) -> None:
346:     """Record a turn, tolerating a duplicate retry and never breaking the reply."""
347:     if memory is None or conversation_id is None or not content.strip():
348:         return
349:     try:
350:         turns = memory.list_turns(conversation_id)
351:         if turns and turns[-1].role == role and turns[-1].content == content:
352:             return
353:         memory.append_turn(conversation_id, role, content)
354:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
355:         return

365:     """Yield the frames of one turn, raising ``_TurnFailure`` on a fatal error."""

367:     def frame(event: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
368:         return _sse(event, {**data, "request_id": request_id})

383:         updated = memory.get_conversation(conversation_id) or conversation

The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.

The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
"""

import json

class _FakeClient:
    payloads: dict[str, Any] = {}
    error: Exception | None = None
    calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []

    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        self.url = url

    async def __aenter__(self) -> _FakeClient:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
        return False

    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error
        payload = str(self.payloads.get(name, "[]"))
        # FastMCP hands back a CallToolResult, whose str() is a repr.
        return SimpleNamespace(content=[SimpleNamespace(text=payload)])


class _ResultClient:
    """A client whose ``call_tool`` returns a real ``CallToolResult``.

    ``fastmcp.Client.call_tool`` returns a ``CallToolResult`` object, not a
    string, so ``str(result)`` is its ``repr``. Stubbing the client with a plain
    string hid that, which is how the canvas hydration silently fell back to
    seed data in production.
    """

    payloads: dict[str, Any] = {}
    error: Exception | None = None
    calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []

    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        self.url = url

    async def __aenter__(self) -> _ResultClient:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
        return False

    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> CallToolResult:
        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error
        text = str(self.payloads.get(name, "[]"))
        return CallToolResult(
            content=[TextContent(type="text", text=text)],
            structured_content={"result": text},
            meta=None,
        )

Check for skills. | | "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. | | "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. | | "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. | | "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. | | "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. | | "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. | | "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent it. | | "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. | ## Platform Adaptation If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions: - Kiro: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/kiro-tools.md` - Freebuff: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` - Claude Code: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/claude-code-tools.md` - Codex: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/codex-tools.md` - Pi: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/pi-tools.md` - Antigravity: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/antigravity-tools.md` - Hermes Agent: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/hermes-tools.md` - Muse: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/muse-tools.md` ## User Instructions User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to. ## Kiro Tool Mapping Skills speak in actions, not tool names. On Kiro CLI they resolve as follows: | Action skills request | Kiro CLI equivalent | | --- | --- | | Invoke or load a skill | Read the skill's `SKILL.md` with the `read` tool and follow its instructions directly | | Create a todo / mark one complete | `todo_list` (create, add, complete, remove commands) | | Read a file | `read` tool (Line or Directory mode) | | Create or overwrite a file | `write` tool (create command) | | Edit a file in place | `write` tool (strReplace command) | | Delete, move, or rename a file | `shell` tool (`rm`, `mv`) | | Run a shell command | `shell` tool | | Search file contents | `grep` tool (regex pattern search) | | Search by symbol / semantic code search | `code` tool (search_symbols, pattern_search, etc.) | | Find files by name | `glob` tool | | List a directory | `read` tool (Directory mode) | | Fetch a URL | `web_fetch` tool | | Search the web | `web_search` tool | | Ask your human partner a question | Respond to the user in your message | | Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | `subagent` tool with a `kiro_default` stage (blocking mode) | | Enter plan mode | `todo_list` to track steps; write designs to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD--design.md` | | Persist progress across compaction | Write the ledger and briefs under `.superpowers/sdd//` (see `executing-plans`) | Skills live in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`. Kiro has no automatic skill-loading tool — read a `SKILL.md` with the `read` tool before following it. For the full Kiro tool reference including subagent dispatch patterns and git worktree instructions, read `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/kiro-tools.md`. ## Project Instructions - Read `.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md` for the ODI domain guardrails, MCP conventions, testing strategy, and README maintenance rules. - Keep `README.md` current in the same task whenever code, commands, dependencies, or capabilities change. - Architecture and data-flow details live in `docs/architecture/`; update them when the package graph or runtime boundaries change. - Superpowers artifacts belong under `docs/superpowers/`: designs in `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD--design.md`, plans in `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-.md`. - Run `uv run pytest` from the root; see `.agents/workflows/test.md` and `docs/architecture/testing.md` for focused commands.

# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, the CLI tree, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | <<<<<<< HEAD | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | ||||||| parent of af849564 (feat(studio): make the desktop app update itself) | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** hands a new user off to the context conversation or straight to a surface. | ======= | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** hands a new user off to the context conversation or straight to a surface. Installed desktop builds **update themselves** in the background and apply on restart. | >>>>>>> af849564 (feat(studio): make the desktop app update itself) | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page. The artwork is original, generated by a committed script, and documented in [brand/README.md](brand/README.md). ```bash uv run python brand/tools/render.py # regenerate every Odi asset ``` ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---
*Let's build AI that builds what people actually need.*

If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent it. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

| List a directory | `read` tool (Directory mode) |
